results.reason: TRS can represent transaction intents and commits with full auditability, but strict isolation/locking and rollback semantics require profile-layer transaction protocol.
Controller loops naturally map to observation-driven intentions and authorized commitments with replayable reconciliation trails.
Commits, merges, and branch intentions map directly; conflict visibility aligns with merge conflict semantics.
TRS can model connection-state coordination and packet-delivery commitments, but transport timing/retransmission/window control are protocol-layer mechanics.
Consent, delegation, and token issuance events are modelable, but cryptographic token lifecycle and protocol handshakes remain profile-layer standards.
Filing, testimony, rulings, and obligations map to O/I/C with authorization and replayable legal provenance.
Scheduling decisions and resource intents are representable, but hard real-time deadlines and CPU dispatch internals remain execution-layer logic.
